content.title: About
content.content: Waffle Fruit is a hybrid dessert consisting of a thin, crisp waffle infused with natural fruit puree (commonly mango, strawberry or passion fruit). It combines the sweetness of fruit with the light texture of a waffle, making it a popular snack and dessert.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Waffle Fruit first appeared in Japan in the early 2000s as part of street‑food culture.
A special press simultaneously bakes the waffle and injects the fruit puree, creating a seamless filling.
More than 20 flavor variants exist, ranging from classic strawberry to exotic passion‑fruit‑lime.
It is often served with toppings such as dried fruit, nuts or edible flowers.
In some countries it is used as a base for ice‑cream sandwiches.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: The fruit puree provides vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The thin waffle is baked with minimal oil, resulting in a modest fat content.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Fruit puree adds dietary fiber that aids normal digestion.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Berries and tropical fruits used in the puree are high in antioxidants that combat free radicals.

items.title: Quick energy snack
items.content: Simple carbs from the waffle and natural sugars from the fruit quickly replenish energy.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Fruit puree can contain a notable amount of natural sugars, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Fruit allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to specific fruits used in the puree.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: While not fatty, the product’s calories can add up due to sugar and starch.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Commercial versions may contain preservatives and artificial flavorings.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Waffle Fruit can be enjoyed straight out of the package, split in half and topped with yogurt, ice cream or nut crumble. It also works well for dessert sandwiches, layered cakes, and fusion‑style culinary creations.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store Waffle Fruit in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2‑3 days. For longer shelf life (up to 1 week) keep it refrigerated. Discard if any mold appears or the taste changes.
